skill.name: xlsx
skill.description: Create, edit, analyze, format, and validate Excel workbooks with pandas, openpyxl, and LibreOffice formula recalculation.
skill.summary: Build reliable spreadsheets with formulas, formatting, analysis, and formula error checks.
skill.author: ArtemisAI

security_audit.summary: The subprocess and Markdown backtick detections are false positives because commands use fixed argument arrays and documentation does not execute. The script still makes a confirmed persistent change to the user LibreOffice profile by creating and overwriting an executable macro module.

remediation.issue: The recalculation setup can overwrite Module1.xba in the user LibreOffice profile.
remediation.suggestion: Use an isolated temporary LibreOffice profile or a nonpersistent UNO workflow. Never replace an existing macro module without explicit consent and backup.

remediation.issue: LibreOffice execution lacks a direct Python timeout on Windows and macOS without gtimeout.
remediation.suggestion: Pass the requested limit through subprocess.run timeout on every platform and terminate child processes after expiration.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete Cross-Platform Timeout Enforcement
semantic_findings.description: LibreOffice can run without an enforced timeout on Windows or macOS systems lacking gtimeout, allowing a malformed workbook to hold the process indefinitely.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work often requires careful formulas, formatting, and validation across many sheets. This skill guides creation, editing, analysis, recalculation, and formula error checks.
actual_capabilities: Create Excel workbooks with formulas, formatting, column widths, and multiple sheets using openpyxl.
Read and analyze workbook data with pandas, including summaries, data types, missing values, and selected columns.
Modify cells, rows, columns, and sheets while following an existing workbook style.
Apply documented financial model conventions for formulas, colors, number formats, assumptions, and source notes.
Recalculate formulas with LibreOffice and report common Excel errors with worksheet locations.
limitations: Formula recalculation requires a local LibreOffice installation and runs an external process.
The recalculation script changes the user LibreOffice profile by installing a persistent macro module.
The documented recalculation workflow targets Linux and macOS; Windows timeout behavior is incomplete.
Large workbooks may require significant memory and time because verification scans every populated cell.

use_cases.title: Build a Financial Model
use_cases.description: Create a formula-driven workbook with separate assumptions, consistent period formulas, source notes, and financial formatting.

use_cases.title: Update an Operations Template
use_cases.description: Add current data and formulas to an established workbook while preserving its sheets, styles, and conventions.

use_cases.title: Analyze Spreadsheet Data
use_cases.description: Inspect multiple sheets, summarize distributions, identify missing values, and export a clear analysis workbook.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excel workbook from the provided table. Format headers, add a total row with formulas, and save it as [filename].

prompt_templates.title: Analyze and Summarize Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [workbook] for missing values, duplicates, and trends. Add a summary sheet with key metrics while preserving source data.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an Existing Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Update [workbook] using [changes]. Preserve existing styles and formulas, document modified assumptions, then verify all references and formula results.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Advanced Financial Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a three-statement financial model from [inputs]. Use separate assumptions, linked formulas, source notes, sensitivity cases, and industry-standard formatting. Recalculate and eliminate formula errors.

output_examples.input: Create a monthly expense workbook with categories, budgets, actual spending, and variance calculations.
output: An Expenses sheet contains the supplied monthly records with clear headers and consistent currency formats.
A Summary sheet totals budget, actual spending, and variance by category using workbook formulas.
Formula validation reports no common Excel errors.

output_examples.input: Update the sales forecast template with actual results and preserve its existing style.
output: Actual results are added to the requested periods without changing established layouts or styles.
Forecast formulas reference separate assumption cells and continue consistently across future periods.
Updated hardcodes include source notes where supporting information was provided.

output_examples.input: Analyze a workbook containing regional order data and create a management summary.
output: The analysis identifies missing values, duplicate records, data types, and regional performance totals.
A management summary presents key metrics in a separate sheet while retaining the original data.
The delivered workbook uses stable number formats and readable column widths.

best_practices: Keep assumptions in dedicated cells and reference them from formulas.
Test sample formulas and edge cases before applying changes across a workbook.
Work on a copy, preserve the established template, and verify formula errors before delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not replace formulas with Python-calculated hardcoded results when the workbook must remain dynamic.
Do not save a workbook loaded with data-only mode because formulas can be lost.
Do not overwrite an existing template style with unrelated standardized formatting.

faq.question: Which spreadsheet formats does this skill address?
faq.answer: The guidance focuses on Excel workbooks and also describes reading tabular data through pandas workflows.

faq.question: Can it calculate Excel formulas with openpyxl alone?
faq.answer: No. Openpyxl stores formulas but does not evaluate them, so the workflow uses LibreOffice for recalculation.

faq.question: Does formula recalculation require extra software?
faq.answer: Yes. LibreOffice must be installed and accessible through the soffice command.

faq.question: Will existing workbook formatting be preserved?
faq.answer: The instructions prioritize existing template conventions, but complex Excel features should be reviewed after modification.

faq.question: How are formula errors checked?
faq.answer: The recalculation script scans workbook cells for common Excel error values and reports their worksheet locations.

faq.question: Does the skill change local application settings?
faq.answer: Yes. The provided recalculation script installs a macro module in the user LibreOffice profile, which presents a security and overwrite risk.
